workflow: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a crisp monochrome IKEA-like electronics assembly instruction illustration sheet, landscape 3:2, pure white background, black technical line art, sparse light gray only, no gradients, no shadows, no color. Four isolated numbered panels in a 2 by 2 grid with broad white gutters and NO borders. Panel 1: two hands align a thin stainless solder-paste stencil flat over an UNPOPULATED rectangular circuit board, stencil taped as a hinge on the left. Panel 2: one hand pulls a flat plastic squeegee across the stencil with a small bead of solder paste. Panel 3: tweezers place a tiny two-terminal surface-mount component onto two paste deposits on a board, enlarged clear view. Panel 4: rectangular PCB with ONLY low-profile SMT parts sits level on a rectangular electric reflow hot plate; then a small arrow to the same PCB on a heatproof bench cooling, no hands touching. Add only numbers 1,2,3,4 above their panels. No other text, no temperature figures, no wall plugs or powered electronics, no through-hole parts, no soldering iron, no fake scientific symbols. Diagram is conceptual technique, not exact board geometry. Keep large clear silhouettes and generous margins for grayscale laser printing.
iron: Use case: scientific-educational. Black and white assembly guide illustration sheet, landscape 3:2, pure white background, crisp technical outline drawing like a furniture assembly manual. Two isolated panels left and right with broad white gutter. LEFT panel: a through-hole axial diode and its two leads fitted into two holes of a circuit board, diode band visible on one end, shown in a clear small side/isometric view. Below it, a second view of board flipped over with iron tip touching both metal pad and component lead, separate thin solder wire feeding into their junction. RIGHT panel: board is held safely by an adjustable nonconductive PCB holder with populated tall components hanging clear below; diagonal cutters trim protruding leads close above their solder fillets, enlarged detail inset. Make exactly one iron and one separate solder wire, keep hands away from hot tip. No soldering on a hot plate. No sparks or smoke, no text except small panel numerals 5 and 6. No invented PCB layout or connector wiring. White and black line art only, sparse gray, printable.
iron_edit: Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct only the inconsistent component positioning in this black-and-white two-panel soldering instruction illustration. Keep the 5 and 6 labels, page layout, iron and separate solder-wire technique, cutter and holder composition, white background and clean monochrome line art. In panel 6, the PCB is flipped bottom-up for trimming soldered leads. Therefore REMOVE the axial diode currently drawn ON TOP of that board; put it hanging BELOW the board instead, with its two leads entering from below and two short soldered lead stubs above. ALL component bodies must be below the board in the trimming view. In the lower soldering view of panel 5, replace the hanging cylindrical vertical component with the SAME horizontal axial diode mounted below the board, its bent leads through two holes from below. Keep the upper panel5 diode placement view unchanged. Ensure exactly the same logical horizontal diode assembly in all three views. No other changes.
smt_identification: Use case: scientific-educational. Create an electronics component identification illustration plate for a black-and-white bench assembly guide. Landscape 3:2, pure white background, crisp fine black technical line art, minimal light gray, no solid black backgrounds. Six generously spaced cells in a 3-column by 2-row grid. Only text is small numbers 1 through 6 in the upper-left of each cell. 1: two separate little rectangular chip passives, one flat black-top resistor with silver end caps and one plain ceramic capacitor with silver end caps; no body markings. 2: a molded surface-mount diode with two end terminations and one visibly broad cathode band. 3: one SOT-23 transistor, EXACTLY three legs: two on near side, one centered far side. 4: a small SOT-23-6 IC, EXACTLY three legs each long side, small circular pin-1 identifier near one corner, no code text. 5: narrow fine-pitch IC body with EXACTLY five gullwing leads each long side, 10 total, small pin-1 corner dot, no code. 6: a square molded shielded power inductor, 5mm class, flat top with no markings, two metal terminals at opposite bottom edges. View all objects three-quarter isometric and clearly recognizable, no boards, no extra pins, no brand logos, no rulers. These are generic package appearances, not exact part drawings. Keep objects large and avoid photorealistic shading.
through_hole_identification: Use case: scientific-educational. Black-and-white electronics assembly component identification sheet, crisp thin black outlines and very light gray fill, pure white background, landscape 3:2. Six clean numbered cells in 3 columns and 2 rows. Draw large recognizable isometric silhouettes, generic not exact dimensioned drawings; only text is small numerals 1 to 6 upper-left. Cell1: TWO separate axial parts, a cylindrical fusible resistor with NO color bands and an axial diode with ONE dark cathode band, bent wire leads left and right. Cell2: TWO separate objects, an upright epoxy-coated disc MOV with exactly two staggered wire leads going downward, beside an upright rectangular box film capacitor with exactly two leads downward; no codes. Cell3: a rectangular sealed PCB power relay with five long through-hole pins on underside, no visible internalmechanism or markings. Cell4: a large rectangular encapsulated AC/DC power module, plain closed case, four underside wire pins near corners (two input and two output), no vent slots, screws or labels. Cell5: two-position right-angle screw PCB terminal block, two top screw heads, two forward-facing wire entrances and two downward solder tails. Cell6: TWO separate parts, a small round domed 3mm through-hole LED on two unequal wire leads beside a square 6mm pushbutton with round plunger and four bent through-hole legs. No circuitboards, no wiring diagrams, no brand logos, no dense texture or shadows. Sparse construction line detail, generous printable white space.

Also lighten the broad dark gray fill on the relay and power module to very light gray while preserving black outline edges to save printer toner. The result remains a monochrome generic package-identification illustration, not a footprint drawing.
